subject: APPEAL of Erroneous Decision from SLC Parking Enforcement - PH5085677
comment: Dear Hearing Officer HO103, I have a "green vehicle permit." The permit is # 1972. Ms. Luna sent it to me. What I was told by the City is that I could use the permit to park for up to 2 hours at a time. Apparently this is an effort from the City to encourage and/or reward adoption of EV's, which contribute less to the terrible pollution in the City. I installed the permit in the back window of my vehicle, exactly as instructed. However, despite this, yesterday I received a $36 citation when I attempted to park in a SLC metered stall for one hour in the morning. When I nicely appealed the erroneous citation, an unknown hearing officer stated: "AFTER REVIEWING ALL THE INFORMATION FROM BOTH PARTIES AS WELL AS THE PHOTOS IN THE MATTER, WE HAVE DETERMINED THIS IS A VALID CITATION AND WOULD NOT BE ABLE TO DISMISS. YOU MUST HAVE AND PROPERLY DISPLAY A VALID GREEN STICKER TO PARK AT METERS FOR FREE FOR UP TO 2 HOURS. YOU HAVE 7 DAYS TO PROVIDE US PROOF YOU HAVE CORRECTED YOUR FAILURE TO DISPLAY VIOLATION OF YOUR PERMIT AND WE WILL REDUCE TO 10.00 YOU MUST SEND A PICTURE OF YOUR STICKER CORRECTLY ATTACHED TO THE REAR WINDOW IN THE PROPER LOCATION TO HEARINGS@SLC.GOV AND WE WILL REDUCE THE FINE AMOUNT." None of the above is true. My sticker was properly placed on my vehicle, as per the attached pictures. It has always been there. My vehicle is a hatchback and the sticker may not be immediately visible to inattentive observers. The initial picture taken by the parking ticket attendant is from far away, but the sticker is nonetheless evident even in the parking ticket attendant's photo. I am not sure that any of this process is the best use of time for city employees or for me. If the City wants to erroneously give tickets to people participating in its Green Vehicles program, then maybe consider just disbanding the program? I ask that the City please advise me as to all further appellate rights, if necessary I will pay the full citation and then sue the City for misrepresenting the nature of the Green Vehicles program. If there is some further need to exhaust remedies at the City level, please kindly advise me on the City's perception of the correct procedures. Incidentally, experiences like this are why I have moved my business out of downtown. Best Regards, Chad -- Chad S. Pehrson

subject: Property Tax Relief for Seniors
comment: An update. On Tuesday afternoon, the Salt Lake County Council voted to oppose McCay's SB 197 and support Harper's SB 224. Unanimous on both. Also spoke on Monday to Millcreek City Mayor Silvestrini and he will also be sending a letter. Thank you.

Mayor Mendenhall, The city is already spending over $40,000,000 on policing homelessness and apparently you feel that's not getting the job done. How many more officers and how much more money do you think it will take to successfully implement something that works. Firing loyal people is not a solution. Oh... I keep forgetting that policing is not a solution. Policing... and then even more policing... may be necessary because all those programs we are spending even more millions on may not be doing what we say they are. Hmm. If they were really working ... we would need less policing. I'm confused. Maybe I'm just old and losing it... but I just can't seem to make sense of all this. Is this a creative new form of self-serving math? Spend more, nothing changes and call it all a success. 2 + 2 = 22 Bernie
